utterances.text: They did, and I said that there were no looted goods that I saw, nor did I hear about it, nor did anyone bring any such goods.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: That's very good, Witness 129. So the investigator asked you to explain how looted goods were shared, which means that somebody looted the goods.

utterances.speaker: B-129 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They asked me whether anybody did any looting and whether I saw anything, and I said that I hadn't seen or heard or seen any goods.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I see. So they suggested to you that they had been involved in looting.

utterances.speaker: B-129 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They didn't suggest anything. They just asked me a question about it, as they did regarding everything else. There were no suggestions by the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So you don't think it's a leading question if I ask you how did you share the looted goods? Surely that implies that you did some looting.

utterances.speaker: B-129 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't call it a suggestion; I would call it lack of knowledge or misinformation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that the task of the military police formed by the Guards was to prevent stealing, looting, and disorder?

utterances.speaker: B-129 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And did you explain that to them?

utterances.speaker: B-129 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So I think that you owe this to your dead commander so that his name shouldn't be slandered and that things should not be attributed to him that he didn't do.

utterances.speaker: B-129 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't owe him anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Since you know everything about the SDG, tell me, what was the relationship between Arkan and his men, if they committed any kind of offence, stealing, or any kind of offence?

utterances.speaker: B-129 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean towards the officers or generally?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Both.

utterances.speaker: B-129 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The punishment was severe, between 50 and 100 lashes on the backside.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, it's -- it's now almost 2.29. I will allow you one more question. We now discover that we have to leave the building altogether at 3.00. The building is going to close until Tuesday morning. Therefore, in order for everyone to have enough time to get out... Mr. Tapuskovic, I'm afraid we'll have to forego your cross-examination. Mr. Milosevic, one more question, if you want.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. If it's just one question: Witness, you explained that every document which was kept in the premises -- You're not hearing me?

utterances.speaker: B-129 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, could you repeat the question? I didn't hear the beginning.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You explained that every document, every written piece of paper which was kept in the premises of the SDG or in the Serbian Unity Party, was destroyed every evening.

utterances.speaker: B-129 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, or the next day.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Or the next day. I see. Tell me, please, how is it then that your entire diary was never destroyed? Or maybe no one considered this to be a serious document?

utterances.speaker: B-129 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They knew of my notebook. But when I left, no one asked me to leave it there. I took it with me. It was my personal agenda in which I kept my notes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I see. Your personal agenda.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: There we are. We've got the answer, and we cannot go on. It is now 2.30, I note. I'm sorry, Mr. Tapuskovic, that we can't allow your cross-examination, and no re-examination either.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can be very brief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think it would be useful.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I'm sure it would be, but circumstances are against us. In particular, it's necessary to get the accused out of the building.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Several things were omitted which are very important for you, Your Honours, for the Judges.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Well, you can put it into writing, if you want. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Witnesses for Monday week, in light of administrative problems, slightly changed. Can I just give the list so that the accused can prepare over the weekend?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: B-14 -- if he'd like to write it down, because there's no way he's going to get a written version today, there's no procedures, I think. B-1489, followed by C-48, followed by B-108, followed by Patrick Ball, followed by Dzevad Guzic, followed by {redacted}.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well. That will be Monday week. But we'll begin with administrative matters, to deal merely with the witnesses. And let me give this ruling so that the parties -- now, I won't give it in any detail. It follows from our earlier rulings, and the same principles apply. It deals with these witnesses: C-1072, 1073, 1102, 1160, 1166, 1186, 1192, 1202, 1205. These witnesses will all be admitted Rule 92 bis, although four of them were identified as part live by the Prosecution. Their statements will all be admitted. All must be available for cross-examination for the reasons which we've set out in our earlier reasons.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. May.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, time is against us. Now, what is it?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll just take up ten seconds. On the transcript there's a number that's not complete. I'd like to just check out the order of witnesses, whether I've got it noted down correctly by listening to it. B-1489 is the first one; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And then 14 -- C-48, B-108, Patrick Ball, Dzevad Guzic, [redacted]; right?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Witness B-129, we shouldn't forget to thank you for coming to the Tribunal to give your evidence. It is concluded, and you're free to go.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: at 2.34 p.m., to be reconvened on Monday, the 28th day of April, 2003, at 9.00 a.m.
